label: FP
reason: The vulnerability report cites insecure randomness from nextFloat(), but the resulting random value is immediately processed via substring(2) to generate a rememberMeKey used only in a secure session management context. The generated key is never directly exposed to users or injected into HTML output. There is no evidence of user input reaching a DOM sink through XSS. All user inputs are properly sanitized and filtered prior to being used in the application logic.

evidence.note: Randomness source is used to generate a rememberMeKey which is then stored in a cookie and used only within session attributes and secure HTTP-only cookies, not in any user-facing output.

XSS warning incorrectly flags getValue() and getName() calls as sources feeding into a concatenation sink, but these operations occur only during cookie parsing and are not rendered in any response body; the output is fully controlled and sanitized via standard Java mechanisms.
